summary: Regional reporting adds a pre-Arafat Tunis meeting with PLO official Yasir Abd Rabbuh and says the 13 February 1989 Arafat meeting addressed US-PLO dialogue and occupied-territory human rights.
detail: FBIS-NES-89-028 preserved a 12 February 1989 Arabic Voice of the PLO broadcast saying Yasir Abd Rabbuh had received Owens in Tunis 'last night,' placing Owens there before the already documented 13 February Arafat meeting. FBIS-NES-89-032 translated Al-Bayan's report that Arafat met Owens on 13 February about the Palestinian view of peace and developing the US-PLO dialogue. Revue d'etudes palestiniennes no. 32, p. 154, characterized Owens as conducting a subcommittee fact-finding visit and added human rights in the occupied territories to the agenda. The Arabic originals are not reproduced in the FBIS scans. No source names a traveling companion.
source_quote: PLO chief Yasir ‘Arafat in Tunis on 13 February met with Wayne Owens

summary: Amman broadcasts fix Wayne Owens's meetings with Prime Minister Zayd al-Rifai and King Hussein to 30 March 1989, with the king meeting at the Royal Court that afternoon.
detail: FBIS-NES-89-061 preserved two English-language broadcasts dated 30 March 1989. Amman Domestic Service said Prime Minister Zayd al-Rifai conferred with Owens in his office that morning about Middle East developments, peace efforts, and bilateral relations. Amman Television said King Hussein received Owens at the Royal Court that afternoon about an international Middle East peace conference. This refines the Jordan stop within the 23 March to approximately 5 April four-country trip. Neither item names or mentions a traveling party.
source_quote: His Majesty King Husayn received at the Royal Court this afternoon U.S. Congressman Wayne Owens

summary: Iraqi state news recorded Wayne Owens and an unnamed accompanying delegation meeting First Deputy Premier Taha Yasin Ramadan in Baghdad on 14 December 1988.
detail: An English-language Iraqi News Agency dispatch preserved in FBIS-NES-88-241 says Taha Yasin Ramadan met Owens and the delegation accompanying him in Baghdad on 14 December 1988. The U.S. ambassador attended. The discussion covered bilateral relations, Iraq's position on the Palestine question, and support for the PLO. This adds an exact meeting to the official 7-22 December 1988 itinerary, but identifies no delegate.
source_quote: Wayne Owens, member of the U.S. Congress External Affairs Committee and the delegation accompanying him.

summary: Jordanian and Syrian broadcasts establish a previously undated Wayne Owens trip through Amman and Damascus on 14-16 December 1989, leaving only one unresolved 1989-90 Middle East trip slot.
detail: FBIS-NES-89-240 translated an Amman broadcast saying King Hussein received Wayne Owens and his delegation at the Royal Hashemite Court on the afternoon of 14 December 1989, with the court chief and U.S. ambassador present. FBIS-NES-89-241 translated Damascus broadcasts saying Vice President Abd al-Halim Khaddam received Douglas Wayne Owens and his accompanying delegation at 1100 on 16 December, and Foreign Minister Faruq al-Shar also received him that morning with the U.S. ambassador present. The House biography confirms Douglas Wayne Owens is Wayne Owens's full name. Linking the two dates as one regional trip and using it to fill a count-derived slot is a synthesis; no delegate is named.
source_datasets: U.S. House History, Art and Archives
source_quote: His Majesty King Husayn this afternoon received U.S. Congressman Wayne Owens and his delegation at the Royal Hashemite Court.

summary: Contemporaneous reporting says a planned December 1989 meeting between Wayne Owens and Syrian President Hafez al-Assad was canceled after Owens lectured Syrian officials on the U.S. commitment to Israel.
detail: The Detroit Jewish News reported on 29 December 1989 that Owens met high-level Syrian officials during a recent trip in preparation for an Assad meeting, but gave a stern lecture about the U.S. commitment to Israel's survival and the Assad meeting was canceled. This is Capitol Hill-sourced contemporaneous journalism, not a Syrian primary record. It adds an intended but unrealized meeting to the newly dated December 1989 trip and names no companion.
source_quote: And as a result, Owens' meeting with the intractable Assad was canceled.
